haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: They get the generic message again. Nothing is written and no email is sent, because the count is already 3 or more.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes from issue. A successful reset or a newer link's request ends it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link is untouched and still usable. The form stays, and the user can retry until the link expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All the account's sessions are deleted, including the resetting device. The user is redirected to login and must sign in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times, then logs the job and user IDs, drops the job, and raises an alert. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and placed only in the encrypted email job, which the worker sends. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: The API hashes the token with SHA-256 and looks up that hash via the unique index. It then checks used_at and revoked_at are null and expires_at is later than now.
haiku-low.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table, counting the user's rows with created_at in the last 60 minutes. A cleanup job deletes rows older than 60 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: Before the new token is inserted, all of the account's unused active links are revoked, in the same transaction, when the count is under 3.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: password_hash update, this token's used_at, all other open tokens' used_at, sessions deleted, and the notice job queued. The notice is queued before commit.
haiku-low.q12: Each submit locks the token row with SELECT FOR UPDATE and rechecks it is active. The second waits, finds it used, rolls back, and gets the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no email is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count of tokens created in the rolling hour is already 3 or more, so the API returns the same generic message. Nothing is written and no email is sent.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from issue. It ends sooner if it is used (burned), revoked by a newer link, or the account's other tokens are burned by a successful reset.
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still active. The API returns 422 with the reason, the token is untouched, the form stays, and the user can retry until the link expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All the account's sessions rows are deleted, including the device that did the reset, and no session cookie is set. The user is redirected (302) to /login and logs in again.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries with backoff up to 3 times. After 3 failures it logs the job id and user id (never the link), drops the job and raises an alert. The user is not told. The user saw the generic message, and the link stays unused until it expires.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is put in the link inside the email job payload, which is created in the same transaction as the hash. The payload is encrypted at rest. The worker sends it, and the payload is deleted once the job is sent or dropped.
sonnet.q8: It computes SHA-256 of the token T from the URL and looks up password_reset_tokens by token_hash (unique index). The link is good if used_at and revoked_at are null and expires_at is after now. Otherwise it shows the expired page.
sonnet.q9: It is not a stored counter. It counts the account's rows in password_reset_tokens with created_at within the last 60 minutes. A cleanup job deletes rows older than 60 minutes, so older requests drop out of the window.
sonnet.q10: Within the request transaction, after the account row is locked and the count is under 3, the API sets revoked_at on the account's active (unused) links. Then it inserts the new token and queues the email job.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the users.password_hash update, used_at on this token, used_at on all the user's other unused tokens, deletion of all the user's sessions, and queuing the "password changed" email job. All commit together, and the email job is queued in the same transaction, not after it.
sonnet.q12: The submit transaction takes a row lock on the token row with SELECT FOR UPDATE and re-checks that it is active. The second request waits, then finds it no longer active, rolls back and shows the expired page. Only one commit happens.
